metaDescription: Six commercial ice makers compared by daily output, bin storage, drain and water inlet needs, ETL certification and fit for bars, cafes and busy homes.
expertTake: The EUHOMY 400 lb machine with a 250 lb bin is the sensible commercial pick for a cafe or small bar, since it matches output to storage. The VEVOR 150 lb unit is the step into commercial ice for a busy home or tiny shop. Skip the 600 lb class unless you actually move that much ice, because the bigger machines need more water, more drain and more space than most buyers plan for.
introParagraphs: A commercial ice maker is built to run all day and every day, not for a few batches before dinner. It uses a larger compressor, a proper drain and usually a bin that holds the day's ice in a cold, insulated space, which is what separates it from a countertop machine.

The buying question is rarely how much ice a machine can make, but how much a business needs at its peak and how that ice is stored. We rank the field by the match between output and storage, the plumbing the machine demands and the build details that decide whether it survives years of daily service.

products.name: EUHOMY commercial ice maker, 400 lb per day, 250 lb bin, ETL
products.description:
This Euhomy balances production against storage: over 400 pounds a day into a 250 pound stainless bin, which is a ratio a cafe or small bar can use. Ice made overnight is waiting in the morning, and the bin absorbs the lunch rush that a smaller machine would not cover.

The maker says it carries ETL certification and a control panel that is easy to use, and the stainless body suits a wet back-of-house. Freestanding placement means you need floor space with clearance for airflow and a drain run. A commercial machine this size also needs a proper water supply line, usually with a filter.

Compared with the smaller VEVOR units it moves far more ice, and compared with the 580 lb machines it is easier to site. Clean the condenser regularly, sanitize the bin on a schedule and descale the water system, because scale and slime are what shorten a commercial machine's life. Train staff to use a clean scoop kept outside the bin, never a glass, since broken glass in the ice is the worst day a bar can have.
products.bestFor: Cafes and small bars that want output matched to storage.
pros: Over 400 lb per day into a 250 lb bin
Stainless body suits a wet kitchen
cons: Needs plumbing, a drain and floor space
Larger than most homes can accommodate

products.name: VEVOR commercial ice maker, 150 lb per day, 16 to 30 lb storage
products.description:
VEVOR's 150 pound machine is the entry to commercial-style ice for a busy home bar, a food truck or a tiny shop. It makes about 50 cubes per cycle and offers a dual water inlet, so it can take water from a faucet line or from a bottle, a flexibility that matters where plumbing is awkward.

Its storage is the limit: 16 to 30 pounds is modest, so a rush depletes it. It installs under a counter, built in or freestanding, which makes it adaptable. The small bin means production, not storage, is what you rely on during a busy hour.

Compared with the 265 lb VEVOR it makes less and stores less but fits tight spaces. Keep the condenser clean, drain the bin regularly and descale on a schedule.
products.bestFor: Home bars, food trucks and tiny shops with awkward plumbing.
pros: Dual water inlet for faucet or bottled supply
150 lb per day for small-scale use
cons: 16 to 30 lb of storage runs out in a rush
Not suited to a high-volume business

products.name: VEVOR commercial ice maker, 265 lb per day, 55 to 85 lb storage
products.description:
A 265 pound daily rating and a bin that holds 55 to 85 pounds put this VEVOR in the middle: more than a home machine, less than a restaurant unit. It makes about 90 cubes per cycle, and the maker says ETL certification and cyclopentane foam insulation help it hold ice.

The insulation matters because a commercial bin that melts its own ice wastes production. For a cafe or a small restaurant it covers the daily needs of a modest menu. The bin is still small compared with a heavy-service operation, so a lunch rush is the stress test.

Compared with the EUHOMY 400 lb it makes less and stores far less but costs less. Place it with clearance for airflow, set a drain run and clean the condenser each month. Because the bin is small relative to the output, a busy hour is better handled by starting the day with a full bin and keeping the lid closed between scoops.
products.bestFor: Small cafes and restaurants with a modest ice menu.
cons: Bin of 55 to 85 lb is small for heavy service

products.name: EUHOMY commercial under-counter ice maker, 100 lb, 33 lb bin
products.description:
Euhomy's smaller commercial unit makes up to 100 pounds a day, 45 cubes per cycle, and stores 33 pounds in an under-counter body. The maker stresses ETL certification for both commercial and home use, which matters when an inspector or a landlord asks.

It is a good fit for a bar, a break room or a basement, a place where a full-size commercial machine would not fit. The storage is small, so it relies on production through the day. Like every commercial unit it needs a water line and a drain, and gravity drainage means the drain must sit below the machine.

Compared with the VEVOR 150 lb it makes less but offers the clear ETL statement. A commercial machine needs a scheduled bin sanitizing, a clean condenser and a descaled water circuit to pass a health check.
products.bestFor: Under-counter spots in bars, break rooms and basements.
pros: ETL certified for commercial and home use
100 lb per day for small spaces
cons: Needs a water line and a drain

products.name: Tessanovi commercial ice maker, 580 lb per day, 350 lb bin, ETL
products.description:
Tessanovi's 580 pound machine produces 156 cubes per cycle and stores 350 pounds, a combination for a restaurant or a busy bar that serves a lot of drinks. A stainless steel exterior and easy-to-maintain design suit a working kitchen.

The output and the bin are both large, so the machine needs space, a solid water supply and a proper drain. At this scale the water and electricity used are real costs, and a heavy-use setting is needed to justify them. ETL approval gives the usual commercial assurance.

Compared with the EUHOMY 400 lb it makes more and stores more at a higher price and a bigger footprint. Clean the condenser monthly, sanitize the bin and descale the water system.
products.bestFor: Restaurants and bars with heavy drink service.
pros: 350 lb bin with 156 cubes per cycle
cons: Large footprint and heavy water use

products.name: Mojgar commercial ice maker, 680 lb per day, 560 lb bin, ETL
products.description:
The Mojgar is the largest machine in the guide: up to 680 pounds a day and a 560 pound bin, built for busy commercial operations. The maker highlights a warranty that covers both the unit and the compressor, an important statement in a category where the compressor is the costly part.

At this scale the machine is part of the kitchen infrastructure, with a significant water draw, a drain that must handle a lot of meltwater and a footprint that takes up real floor. It makes sense for a restaurant, a hotel kitchen or an event business that needs a large reserve.

Compared with the Tessanovi it makes more and stores more. Keep the condenser clean, schedule bin sanitation and descale regularly, and plan a service relationship.
products.bestFor: High-volume kitchens, hotels and event businesses.
pros: 560 lb bin is the largest here
Warranty covers the unit and compressor
cons: Large footprint and high water use
Far more machine than a small business needs

buyingCriteria.explanation: Daily output is only useful if the bin can hold it until the rush. The EUHOMY 400 lb pairs with a 250 lb bin, while the VEVOR 265 lb has a 55 to 85 lb bin. A machine with a high rating and a tiny bin runs out of ice at the worst moment. Estimate your peak hour, not your daily total.

A bin holds the ice in a cold space, and its insulation decides how much melts. The VEVOR 265 lb lists cyclopentane foam, and the large units list insulated stainless bins. Look for a bin sized to your peak and an insulation story, since a bin that melts its ice wastes production.

Commercial machines need a supply line and a drain, and a pump where gravity will not work. The VEVOR 150 lb offers a dual inlet for faucet or bottled water, a flexibility the others lack. Check where your water and drain are before choosing, since moving plumbing costs more than the machine.

ETL certification shows a unit has been evaluated against a safety standard, which inspectors and insurers often expect. The EUHOMY, VEVOR 265 lb, Tessanovi and Mojgar list it. For a business, a certified machine is easier to get through a health inspection.

A commercial compressor rejects heat into the air, so it needs clearance and a cool room. Placing a machine in a hot, cramped corner cuts output and shortens compressor life. Leave the space the maker specifies and keep the condenser clean.

Hard water coats the evaporator and cuts output. A water filter on the supply line is essential, and a descale schedule is the real maintenance. Test your water with a cheap hardness kit, and budget for filters, because a unit that scales up in the first year is an expensive lesson.

howWeEvaluated.title: Output versus storage
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared daily output, from 100 to 680 pounds, with bin size, from 33 to 560 pounds. A balanced ratio scored best. A big output with a tiny bin scored low for service.

howWeEvaluated.title: Plumbing flexibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at drain and inlet options, including the VEVOR's dual inlet and under-counter installs. A machine that fits awkward plumbing earned credit. Larger units were noted for their demands.

howWeEvaluated.title: Certification and insulation
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted ETL listings and insulation claims such as cyclopentane foam. Certified units scored higher for business use. Insulation affects how much ice survives in the bin.

howWeEvaluated.title: Footprint and build
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered stainless exteriors, under-counter and freestanding options and floor space. Compact machines suit small shops. Large machines were flagged for space and water use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Support and warranty
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for warranty statements, such as the Mojgar's compressor coverage. The compressor is the costliest part. Clear warranty terms scored higher.

cards.label: Under-counter
cards.text: The EUHOMY 100 lb and VEVOR 150 lb fit under a counter and are easy to place. Their bins are small and they rely on production.

cards.label: Freestanding large
cards.text: The EUHOMY 400 lb, Tessanovi and Mojgar make and store far more, with a bigger footprint and heavier plumbing.

howToChoose.note: Under-counter for small spaces; freestanding for real volume.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A large bin, fast cycles and a certified machine. Estimate ice per drink and per peak hour.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The EUHOMY 400 lb and Tessanovi 580 lb fit bars. The VEVOR 150 lb suits a small home bar.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Ice is central to your business. The EUHOMY 400 lb, Tessanovi and Mojgar repay in capacity and warranty.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You need ice a few times a week at home. A countertop machine is cheaper and enough.

maintenance.why: Dust blocks heat rejection and raises compressor load. A brush or vacuum keeps output up, and in a kitchen with grease in the air the coil can need cleaning twice as often as in a clean back room.
A warm, wet bin grows slime. Sanitize it with an approved cleaner and rinse well.

A layer of scale on the evaporator slows freezing and shrinks output. Use a maker-approved cleaner, follow the rinse steps exactly, and discard the first batch of ice afterward so no cleaning residue reaches a customer's glass.
When the filter clogs, flow drops and minerals slip past into the machine. Keep spares on hand.
A blocked drain floods the bin or the floor. Pour water through to confirm flow.

faq.q: How much ice does a business need?
faq.a: Count the ice in a typical drink, multiply by the drinks you serve in your busiest hour and size the bin to cover that hour with a margin. Cocktail menus and blended drinks use far more ice than plain soft drinks. A machine sized only to the daily total will run dry at the rush even when it makes plenty overnight.

It shows the unit was evaluated to a recognized safety standard. Inspectors and insurers often expect it for commercial use. It is a safety listing, not a performance guarantee, so it tells you the wiring and construction passed a review but nothing about how much ice the machine will make in your room.

faq.q: Do I need a drain for a commercial ice maker?
faq.a: Yes in most cases, since melt water and cleaning water must go somewhere. A pump helps if the drain is higher than the machine.

faq.q: Can a commercial machine run at home?
faq.a: Yes, if you have the space, a water line and a drain. Many owners use under-counter units in basements and bars. Check the electrical requirement too, since some larger machines want a dedicated circuit, and ask whether your local rules want an approved drain connection before you install.

faq.q: Why does my commercial ice maker make less ice?
faq.a: Common causes are a dirty condenser, warm water, scale or a hot room. Clean and descale first. Then check that the machine has the clearance the maker specifies on the vented sides, and that the room is not running hot, since a commercial compressor in a closet struggles in a way no cleaning can fix.

faq.q: How long does a commercial ice maker last?
faq.a: With regular cleaning, filters and descaling, many serve for years. Neglect shortens that life far more than heavy use does. The failures that show up first are almost always water side, scale on the evaporator and slime in the bin, and both are cheap to prevent with a filter and a cleaning calendar.
